subject: computer-science
title: OOP: Inheritance and Polymorphism
welcome_lead: Share behaviour cleanly — and let it change shape.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: inheritance, polymorphism, overriding and method dispatch.
final_note: Inheritance shares code; polymorphism varies behaviour.

concepts.def: A class deriving fields and methods from a parent class.
One interface, many forms — same call, different behaviour by type.
A subclass redefining a method declared in a parent class.
The parent class from which another class inherits.
A class that inherits from a parent class.
A class that cannot be instantiated and may declare abstract methods.

walkthroughs.body_html: A subclass inherits from a superclass: Dog extends Animal. The subclass automatically gets fields and methods of the parent and can add or override them.
A reference of type Animal might point to a Dog or a Cat. Calling speak() dispatches to the correct method at runtime — this is polymorphism.
Abstract classes declare methods without implementing them, forcing subclasses to provide details. Shape is abstract; Circle and Square implement area() differently.
